response.title: which power stations keep working while they are charging without wearing out the battery
response.answer:
You're looking for a portable power station with true AC bypass (or pass-through) capability, where you can power connected devices while the station is plugged into the wall, without continuously cycling and wearing out its battery.

The important distinction is that not all power stations with pass-through charging actually bypass the battery.

There are three different designs:

Technology

	

How it works

	

Battery wear




True AC bypass

	

Wall power directly supplies connected AC devices

	

Minimal cycling




Pass-through charging

	

Charges battery while powering devices, potentially involving the battery

	

Depends on design




Online/double-conversion UPS

	

Continuously converts incoming power to DC and back to AC

	

Depends on battery isolation and charging design

For your purpose, true AC bypass with a LiFePO4 (LFP) battery is the combination I'd prioritize.

Even with bypass, keeping an LFP battery at 100% charge for months can accelerate calendar aging. A configurable charge limit of 70–80% is particularly useful.

Shop

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Verified AC bypass

1,024Wh · 1,800W AC output · LFP battery

My first choice for your requirement. EcoFlow explicitly confirms that AC bypass is enabled by default and can be controlled in the app. Its manual describes grid power supplying the AC outputs directly. 
EcoFlow US
+1

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station - 1,024Wh | 2…

$699.99

1,024Wh · 2,000W AC output · LFP battery

Supports UPS operation, but I'd verify its specific AC bypass behavior before buying it for zero-cycle daily use.

BLUETTI AC180 Solar Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,152Wh

$998.00

1,152Wh · 1,800W AC output · LFP battery

Another UPS-capable option, but its pass-through behavior needs confirmation for your particular use case.

How true bypass protects the battery

Normal operation while plugged into AC

Conceptual diagram: after charging is complete, the battery normally does not discharge to supply the AC load while grid bypass is active.

One important caveat: AC bypass applies to AC outlets, not necessarily USB-C or 12V DC outputs. Those may use a different internal power path. And bypass reduces cycling, but doesn't eliminate battery aging entirely.

One question that changes my recommendation

Are you planning to leave the power station plugged into the wall 24/7 as a UPS, or do you want to run devices continuously while charging from solar panels?

Those are quite different electrically, and the best models for avoiding battery wear differ.
